extracted.intended_audience: Authors reporting system-level healthcare quality, safety, value or improvement studies (manuscript authors, improvement scientists, journal editors and reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting guideline for writing and structuring manuscripts that describe system-level efforts to improve healthcare quality, safety, value or related outcomes. Provides 18 items (Title through Funding) specifying what to report in each manuscript section and detailed expectations for methods, context, study design and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate that the manuscript concerns an initiative to improve healthcare (broadly defined to include the quality, safety, effectiveness, patient-centredness, timeliness, cost, efficiency and equity of healthcare).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide adequate information to aid in searching and indexing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarise all key information from various sections of the text using the abstract format of the intended publication or a structured summary such as: background, local problem, methods, interventions, results, conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem description
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature and significance of the local problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Available knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary of what is currently known about the problem, including relevant previous studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Informal or formal frameworks, models, concepts and/or theories used to explain the problem, any reasons or assumptions that were used to develop the intervention(s) and reasons why the intervention(s) was expected to work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SQUIRE 2.0 uses the broader label 'rationale' to encourage explicit reporting of formal and informal theories, models, concepts or hunches as to why the intervention was expected to work. A well thought out rationale should align with appropriate measures and the study of the intervention and may be revisited in the discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose of the project and of this report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context
rubrics_metrics.description: Contextual elements considered important at the outset of introducing the intervention(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context is defined as physical and sociocultural make-up of the local environment (external environmental factors, organisational dynamics, collaboration, resources, leadership, and the interpretation ('sense-making') by professionals, patients and caregivers). SQUIRE 2.0 recognises context as a fundamental item in methods but notes its relevance across the manuscript; authors should describe and acknowledge context rather than control it away and should describe how context influenced design, implementation, measurement and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of the intervention(s) in sufficient detail that others could reproduce it. Specifics of the team involved in the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete description includes inputs, internal activities and outputs (eg, logic model) and mechanisms by which components are expected to produce change. Authors are encouraged to use TIDieR and other detailed intervention description resources as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study of the intervention(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach chosen for assessing the impact of the intervention(s). Approach used to establish whether the observed outcomes were due to the intervention(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes 'doing' improvement from 'studying' it: 'doing' aims to produce local improvements while 'studying' aims to contribute generalisable knowledge. This item focuses on whether and why an intervention 'works' and should align with the rationale; it may include preplanned formal testing of the proposed theory and assessment of the intervention's impact on context. Be transparent, complete and accurate about methods used to study the intervention and the relationship between doing and studying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures chosen for studying processes and outcomes of the intervention(s), including rationale for choosing them, their operational definitions and their validity and reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also include description of the approach to ongoing assessment of contextual elements that contributed to success, failure, efficiency and cost. Describe methods employed for assessing completeness and accuracy of data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative and quantitative methods used to draw inferences from the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe methods for understanding variation within the data, including the effects of time as a variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical aspects of implementing and studying the intervention(s) and how they were addressed, including, but not limited to, formal ethics review and potential conflict(s) of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider potential harms (opportunity costs, invasion of privacy, staff distress) and how these were weighed and managed; report involvement of ethics committees and how conflicts were handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial steps of the intervention(s) and their evolution over time (eg, time-line diagram, flow chart or table), including modifications made to the intervention during the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details of process measures and outcomes; contextual elements that interacted with the intervention(s); observed associations between outcomes, interventions and relevant contextual elements; unintended consequences (unexpected benefits, problems, failures or costs); and details about missing data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Key findings, including relevance to the rationale and specific aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also state particular strengths of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature of the association between the intervention(s) and the outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include comparison of results with findings from other publications; impact of the project on people and systems; reasons for differences between observed and anticipated outcomes including influence of context; and costs and strategic trade-offs, including opportunity costs. Encourage explanation of potential mechanisms by which the intervention resulted (or failed to result) in change to develop explanatory theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits to the generalisability of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe factors that might have limited internal validity such as confounding, bias or imprecision in design, methods, measurement or analysis, and efforts made to minimise and adjust for limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address sustainability, potential for spread to other contexts, implications for practice and further study in the field, and suggested next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources of funding that supported this work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the role, if any, of the funding organisation in the design, implementation, interpretation and reporting.
